paper_diagnosis: Refractory delirium tremens treated with propofol infusion
disease_label_per_paper: Alcohol-withdrawal-induced delirium tremens requiring ICU propofol, intubation, and mechanical ventilation
presentation_summary: 32-year-old man with an 8-year history of heavy alcohol use was admitted for altered mental status and agitation.
He had repeated vomiting, tremors, high-colored urine, loss of appetite, anxiety, hepatomegaly, BP 110/74 mmHg, pulse 94/min, and respiratory rate 20/min.
Initial labs showed AST 126 IU/L and ALT 118 IU/L with fatty liver and hepatomegaly on ultrasound; renal function, coagulation, and electrolytes were reported normal.
Minor withdrawal symptoms were initially controlled with lorazepam 5 mg on day 1, but his condition deteriorated and delirious symptoms appeared on day 3.
He was transferred to ICU, responded poorly to benzodiazepines, and required propofol infusion, intubation, and mechanical ventilation.
